dimensions.detail: The skill's capabilities match its stated wrap-up purpose: checking git state, committing local work, optionally pushing/deploying only under policy, consolidating memory, drafting improvements, and producing a report.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: It uses broad natural-language triggers and defaults to execution mode, so a user should invoke it deliberately or request dry-run mode when they only want a preview.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The package consists of markdown/json instructions and templates with no executable installer, scripts, obfuscated code, or hidden runtime payload.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill may inspect session context, diffs, command output, repository status, and created documents; this is proportionate for a wrap-up skill, and it includes filters against persisting secrets or sensitive personal data.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: It may create commits, move misplaced document files, update CLAUDE.md or scoped rules, and write memory records, but push/deploy/publish are explicitly gated and publishing is draft-only unless requested.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.findings:
[SQP-1] expected: The trigger phrases are common, which could cause accidental invocation, but the advertised purpose is exactly end-of-session wrap-up and the behavior is disclosed rather than hidden.
[SQP-2] expected: Moving document files is a real local side effect and lacks an explicit preview requirement, but it is limited to placement cleanup for files created in the session and fits the shipping workflow.
[SQP-2] expected: Committing local changes is a meaningful repo mutation, but it is disclosed, purpose-aligned, and external push is gated by explicit request or project policy.
llm.guidance: Install only if you want an agent to actively wrap up sessions by making local commits, organizing files, and writing scoped memory. Use dry-run mode first for sensitive repositories, and confirm project policy before allowing pushes, deploys, or publish actions.
llm.summary: This skill is a disclosed end-of-session workflow that can make local repo and memory changes, but its behavior is coherent with its stated purpose and external actions are gated.
